questions.q: Which is the stronger picture?
choices: B; average and level together
A; one clean line reads better
Same; a second line adds nothing
A; a level only adds noise to it
questions.answer: B; average and level together
questions.why: B. On our card, a line many people watch matters, and it is best when an average and a level sit together. B retakes the 50-day and a round 100.00 level that held before the break, while A retakes only the 50-day. Grading is a judgment call, so this is a cue, not a score.
questions.lesson_line: An average and a level together: a stronger line to retake.

wrong.A; one clean line reads better: Two lines taken back at once is the stronger picture, not the noisier one.
wrong.Same; a second line adds nothing: A second line that many people watch adds to the picture.
wrong.A; a level only adds noise to it: A round number that held is a level many people name. Together with an average it is the best case on our card.

questions.story: Two remounts close back over their line today, everything else equal. A retakes the 50-day alone. B retakes the 50-day and the round 100.00 level together. 100.00 held as support for months before the break.
questions.simple: B. A line many people watch counts in its favor, and an average and a level retaken together is the best case.

deeper.trap: The trap is counting lines instead of asking whether they are real. A level must be a real level: it held before it broke, with at least 10 of the 15 closes before the break at or above it. A round number that was chopped through for weeks does not add to the cue.

reasons: grade cues sit against rulebook E50, which says grading is discretionary

questions.q: May you buy?
choices: Yes; the ban covers only 3 sessions
No; wait until after the report
No; a report within 8 sessions bars it
Yes, but only at half the usual size
questions.answer: Yes; the ban covers only 3 sessions
questions.why: Yes. The rule bars new buys only in the 3 sessions before a report. This report is 8 sessions away, so the buy is allowed. If you hold through the report, the trade must be up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Only the last 3 sessions before a report bar the buy.

wrong.No; wait until after the report: The ban covers only the 3 sessions before a report. Eight sessions out is outside it.
wrong.Yes, but only at half the usual size: The report rule is a ban on the last 3 sessions, not a size cut.

questions.story: A clean remount triggers today. The company reports in 8 sessions.
questions.simple: Yes. Only the last 3 sessions before a report are barred, and this report is 8 sessions away.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22, no buys in the 3 days before a report)

questions.q: What is a U&R, an Undercut and Rally?
choices: A dip under a level, back over it fast
A long stay under a line, then a retake
A gap up over a line on heavy volume
A bounce off a line that never broke
questions.answer: A dip under a level, back over it fast
questions.why: A dip under a level, back over it fast. A U&R undercuts the level, fakes out sellers and would-be short-sellers, then rallies back above it. It is bought as the level is retaken.
questions.lesson_line: A U&R dips under the level and takes it right back.

wrong.A long stay under a line, then a retake: That is a Remount. A U&R is back above the level within a few sessions.
wrong.A gap up over a line on heavy volume: A gap is not the setup. A U&R dips under the level first, then rallies back over it.
wrong.A bounce off a line that never broke: A bounce that never broke the line is a pullback. A U&R undercuts the level first.

questions.simple: A U&R dips under a level, then rallies back over it within a few sessions.

reasons: +2 the U&R card names the quick return, a proposed number
+1 new question

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Never buy more than ___ above the buy point.
questions.simple: We never buy more than 4% above the buy point, because chasing cuts the number of shares.
questions.why: 4%. We never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: No more than 4% over the buy point.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (C28)
added so q46 applies a rule taught first

questions.q: We buy a long that sits 15% over its 10-day average when the setup is clean.
questions.answer: False
questions.simple: False. We skip any long more than 10% over its 10-day average, however clean the setup looks.
questions.why: False. We skip a long more than 10% over its 10-day average. That far above its short average, the stock is too stretched to buy, however clean the setup looks.
questions.lesson_line: A clean setup does not excuse a stretched stock.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (C29)
added so q47 applies a rule taught first

questions.q: After a gap down through your stop, what sets the new stop?
choices: The first 30-minute bar's low
The first 5-minute bar's low
The first 60-minute bar's low
The open of the gap-down day
questions.answer: The first 30-minute bar's low
questions.simple: On a gap through the stop, the first 30 minutes decide, and the low of that 30-minute bar is the new stop.
questions.why: The first 30-minute bar's low. On a gap through the stop, the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. That bar's low is the new stop, with a ceiling: past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

wrong.The first 5-minute bar's low: Not our rule. The first 30 minutes decide, not the first 5.
wrong.The first 60-minute bar's low: Not our rule. The rule uses the first 30-minute bar, not the first hour.
wrong.The open of the gap-down day: The open is not the stop. The first 30-minute bar's low is.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B20)
added so q27 applies a rule taught first

questions.story: A leader sits above a rising 200-day. It lost its 50-day, then remounts it on a clear green close. That same close also clears its 20 EMA.
questions.q: How does our card read this remount?
choices: A plus cue, since none sit overhead
B minus cue, since it is stretched
No cue, since only the 50-day counts
Pass, until the 20 EMA is retested
questions.answer: A plus cue, since none sit overhead

wrong.No cue, since only the 50-day counts: This cue counts every average still above price after the remount day: the 20 EMA, the 50-day and the 200-day.
wrong.B minus cue, since it is stretched: Clearing every average is not being stretched. Our stretch rule is more than 10% over the 10-day, and the story gives no such gap.
wrong.Pass, until the 20 EMA is retested: Our card asks for no retest of the 20 EMA. Clearing it on the remount close is part of the cue.

questions.why: A plus cue. Our card proposes that a remount clearing all the averages at once, above a rising 200-day, is an A plus cue. It counts the 20 EMA, the 50-day and the 200-day. After this close, none of the three sits above price. A cue is a hint, not a score, and grading stays a judgment.
questions.lesson_line: No average left overhead after the remount, over a rising 200-day: our card's proposed A plus cue.
questions.simple: Our card proposes that a remount leaving no average above price, over a rising 200-day, is an A plus cue.

reasons: +2 a proposed grade cue on card 32, not an owner ruling
+1 grade cues sit against rulebook E50 (grading is discretionary)

questions.story: The market has a sharp shakeout and the index drops under its own 50-day. A leader loses its 50-day in the same drop but holds above its 200-day. Later it remounts its 50-day on a clear green close, while the index is still under its own.
questions.q: How does our card read the timing of this remount?
choices: An A plus cue: it moved first
A pass: wait for the index to remount
A B minus cue: it fought the market
No cue: the index does not matter
questions.answer: An A plus cue: it moved first

wrong.A pass: wait for the index to remount: Our card does not make a leader wait for the index. Remounting first is its A plus cue, though the market reading still applies.
wrong.A B minus cue: it fought the market: Moving back before the index is strength, not a fault. Our card lists it as an A plus cue.
wrong.No cue: the index does not matter: The index matters on our card. Its best case is after a correction, as the indexes remount their lines and leaders remount first.

questions.why: An A plus cue: it moved first. A leader that lost the line in a market shakeout, then remounted before the index, is our card's A plus cue. Our card says the setup is best after a correction, when leaders remount first. A cue is a hint, not a score.
questions.lesson_line: Leaders remount first. One that beats the index back is an A plus cue on our card.
questions.simple: Our card counts a leader that remounts its line before the index does as an A plus cue.

Where the two cards differ and the unit keys neither side: the slope of the 200-day (card 32 proposes higher than 20 sessions ago, card 13 proposes not falling fast and asks for the 20-session slope only for an A); the reclaim day candle numbers (card 13 asks 0.5 ATR in its scan, card 32 0.25 ATR); the pause (card 32 has the first quiet day arm the buy within 5 sessions, card 13 has the last session of a 1 to 5 session pause be the inside day); whether the close of the remount day is a buy (card 13 picks Entry A when its stop is about 3% or less, card 32 makes the pause the default); the stop anchor (above); the close back under the line after the buy (card 13 settles it with D-136: hold, no extra exit; card 32 leaves it to D-008 but its dossier recommends the same, so q17 keys the substance with card 13's wording); a remount of the 20 EMA (card 32 allows it only above a rising 50-day, card 13 gives it to the Wedge Pop). The 50-day line needs the close above the 200-day on both cards (B26).

The short boundary with the U&R is 3 sessions (the U&R card's proposed ur.inv_no_reclaim) and the long side is 'a week or more'. The glossary closes the gap between them: the U&R family runs to 4 closes and the Remount starts at 5. No question asks about exactly 4 closes.

The walk-throughs call the stop 'a few cents under' (F62). AMD's stop is 3.3% from the buy, just over the 3% line: A13 says the stop usually sits within about 3%, so the walk-through says size follows the stop.
